title: Scenario Experience Spec
description:
Declarative experience contract for a scenario's UI, living in a root `experience/` folder (index.json + pages/*.json + journeys/*.json + components/*.json) that mirrors `requirements/` on the business axis. One schema covers all four document kinds, discriminated by the top-level `kind` field: experience-index, experience-page, experience-journey, experience-component.

DOCTRINE (owned by scenarios/experience-manager, see its docs/internal/DECISIONS.md):

1. CLAIM-BASED, NEVER DESCRIPTIVE. A page or component spec is a set of typed claims about perceivable outcomes ("exactly one action visually dominates"), never an exhaustive description of the surface. The optional `sketch` block is non-normative and exists only for wireframe rendering and BAS scaffolding — it is never validated against the built UI.

2. OPEN-WORLD. The spec is a floor, not a census: anything unclaimed is free, and nothing is ever flagged for being unmentioned. Validators check stated claims plus declared-state coverage only. Every object accepts `x-` prefixed extension properties; the claim `type` vocabulary is open.

3. ENFORCEMENT TIERS. Every claim carries a tier: `machine` (deterministically checkable now — gates CI), `manual` (human-attested with expiry via the attestation ledger), `aspirational` (stated intent with no check yet — advisory only, never rejected). The spec language is allowed to run ahead of the validator; vocabulary grows by promoting aspirational claims to machine as checks are built. `custom`-type claims may not be machine tier (there is nothing deterministic to check).

4. INTENT/BINDINGS SPLIT. Claims and elements are stable intent (role + accessible name, WAI-ARIA vocabulary). The `bindings` block is the volatile grounding (element id -> testid/selector) that implementation refactors may touch freely; it is also the selector SSOT that bas/ case scaffolding reads. Never encode selectors, coordinates, or pixel values in claims.

5. DEPTH IS A LADDER, NOT A GATE. Pages use L0 identity -> L1 priorities -> L2 grounded claims -> L3 state coverage -> L4 journey membership. Components use L0 identity -> L1 priorities -> L2 grounded claims -> L3 example-anchored state coverage. Depth is computed by the experience-manager parser, never stored in these files. A page or component at L1 is compliant; depth is tracked as debt.

What JSON Schema cannot express is enforced by the experience-manager parser: cross-file reference resolution (claim->element, binding->element, journey step->page/state, component state->example, prd_ref->PRD operational target, route->UI), per-array id uniqueness, coverage against DESIGN.md's required UX-state contract, and tier/open-world semantics.

Id.description: Kebab-case identifier, stable once published (other files and bas/ cases reference it).

PrdRef.description: Operational-target id in this scenario's PRD.md. The parser verifies it resolves.

Role.description: WAI-ARIA role (button, link, table, list, listitem, form, region, img, meter, note, alert, status, ...). The parser validates against the ARIA registry. Custom roles are allowed only as x- namespaced extensions where ARIA is insufficient.

StateId.description: Page-state id. Open set. Canonical vocabulary (from DESIGN.md's required UX-state contract): default, loading, submitting, saving, syncing, refreshing, empty, partial, stale, success, validation-error, request-error, permission-denied, offline, retry. Page-specific states (e.g. comparing) are welcome.

Viewport.description: Viewport class. Open set; canonical vocabulary: mobile, tablet, desktop, wide.

Locale.description: BCP-47-style locale tag (en, ja, ar, ...). Reading-order claims are direction-aware: rtl locales flip horizontal expectations.

Tier.description: machine = deterministically checkable now, gates CI. manual = human-attested with expiry. aspirational = stated intent with no check yet; advisory only, never a failure.

PageStatus.description: draft = intent authored ahead of (or out of sync with) the build; reconciliation runs advisory. active = the build is expected to conform; machine-tier claims gate. deprecated = excluded from coverage, pending removal.

pages.description: Registry of page specs. Every file under pages/ must be listed here and vice versa (parser-enforced).

components.description: Registry of reusable component specs whose states are anchored to named catalog examples.

path.description: Path relative to the experience/ folder.

priorities.description: Ranked communication priorities — what this page must convey, in order (rank = array order). Deliberately capped: if everything is a priority, nothing is. This is what saliency scoring (P2) is checked against.

states.description: The perceivable states this page declares. Claims may scope to states; coverage checks compare this list against DESIGN.md's required UX-state contract.

elements.description: Intent-level perceivable things claims refer to. Role + accessible-name expectation only — grounding lives in bindings.

regions.description: Meaningful independently rendered or asynchronously resolved surfaces. Passive primitives inherit their parent region lifecycle and are not declared here.

floorOptOuts.description: Explicit per-page escape hatch for inherited experience floors. Opt-outs must name the floor and carry a human-readable reason.

purpose.description: One or two sentences: what a person should get from this page. Written for a reader, not a parser.

StateSetup.description: Deterministic navigation setup used before capturing a non-default page state. This is deliberately limited to URL shape and settle timing; richer interaction flows belong in BAS cases.

route.description: Optional route override for this state. Omitted means the page's primary route.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the capture URL for this state.

hash.description: URL fragment to apply for this state, with or without the leading #.

settleMs.description: State-specific settle time before the accessibility snapshot.

name.description: Expected accessible name (or a stable substring of it). Compared against the captured accessibility tree during reconciliation.

type.description: Open vocabulary. v1 machine-checkable types (checked against the BAS-captured accessibility tree): element-present, element-absent, single-dominant-action, visible-without-scroll, reading-order (order of `elements` array; direction-aware per locale), state-covered (the state renders dedicated content, not blank/default), state-distinct (two states are distinguishable), keyboard-reachable, affordance-present (params.affordances names required controls such as sort/filter/search, scoped by params.targetRole or the first referenced element role), spacing (two elements plus params.minSeparation), state-contrast (a state, background, and params.minContrastRatio), size-parity (two elements plus optional params.tolerance), and differential (two captured contexts must meet their expected values and differ). `custom` = free-form claim that always parses and may not be machine tier. Unknown types parse and are treated as aspirational until the validator learns them.

statement.description: The claim in plain language, intent-level. Never selectors, coordinates, or pixel values.

elements.description: Element ids this claim refers to. For reading-order, array order is the expected perceptual order.

states.description: States the claim is scoped to. Omitted = holds in every declared state.

reason.description: Why this page intentionally diverges from the inherited floor.

Bindings.description: Volatile grounding: element id -> concrete hooks in the implementation. The only section a pure refactor/restyle should ever touch. Selector SSOT for bas/ case scaffolding.

regions.description: Volatile runtime hooks for declared meaningful regions. Keys are stable region ids; values are selectors or test ids.

selector.description: CSS selector fallback when a testid is not feasible.

required.description: Required unsettled or failed regions block page readiness. Optional failures aggregate to partial while the primary task remains usable.

Sketch.description: NON-NORMATIVE layout hint for wireframe rendering and workshop variants only. Never validated against the built UI; divergence here is not a finding. Regions may reference element ids and coarse positions on an abstract 12-column grid.

claims.description: Journey-level claims (e.g. friction budget). Same claim model; runtime checking is P2 and builds on workflow-health execution.

page.description: Page id declared in this scenario's experience index.

state.description: State declared on that page. Omitted = default.

intent.description: What the user accomplishes or understands at this step.

via.description: The affordance used to arrive here (free text, e.g. an element id or gesture).

priorities.description: Ranked communication priorities for this reusable component.

states.description: Perceivable component states. Each state is anchored to a named catalog specimen.

floorOptOuts.description: Escape hatch for component floors only. Page floors do not apply to component documents.

purpose.description: One or two sentences: what a person should be able to perceive or do with this reusable component.

examplesRef.description: Path from experience/components/ to the catalog component or hook version examples.json that grounds this spec. Adopted scenario components may point at the shared react-component-library catalog.

storyRef.description: Path from experience/components/ to the catalog component or hook version story.json that grounds this spec. Adopted scenario components may point at the shared react-component-library catalog.

extends.description: Exact canonical RCL contract this local component wraps. A wrapper may add behavior but cannot silently replace the pinned lifecycle or claims.

extension.description: Required only for an extends wrapper; explains the additive scenario-local behavior.

example.description: Named example in the referenced examples.json file.

reason.description: Why this component intentionally diverges from the inherited component floor.
